name: Christian de Duve
summary: Belgian cell biologist who discovered lysosomes and peroxisomes, sharing the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

name: Fred Opperdoes
summary: Author of the obituary, affiliated with de Duve Institute and Universite Catholique de Louvain.

name: Albert Claude
summary: Cell biologist and Nobel co-recipient who developed differential centrifugation techniques.

name: George E. Palade
summary: Cell biologist and Nobel co-recipient who collaborated with de Duve in New York.

name: J. P. Bouckaert
summary: Belgian physiologist whose laboratory de Duve joined early in his career.

name: Hugo Theorell
summary: Nobel Prize winner whose laboratory in Stockholm de Duve visited post-war.

name: Gerty Cori
summary: Nobel Prize winner whose laboratory at Washington University de Duve visited.

name: Carl Cori
summary: Nobel Prize winner whose laboratory at Washington University de Duve visited.

name: Earl Sutherland
summary: Nobel Prize winner who collaborated with de Duve at Washington University.

name: Alex B. Novikoff
summary: Researcher at Albert Einstein College of Medicine who collaborated with de Duve on electron micrographs of lysosomes.

name: King Baudouin
summary: King of Belgium who raised de Duve to the rank of Viscount.

name: Julien Doornaert
summary: Photographer credited with the image of de Duve at age 95.

aliases: International Institute of Cellular and Molecular Pathology
name: de Duve Institute
summary: Biomedical institute in Brussels founded by de Duve, originally named ICP.

name: Catholic University of Louvain
summary: Belgian university where de Duve studied and later became professor.

name: Belgian army
summary: Military force where de Duve served as a medical officer during WWII.

name: Nobel Medical Institute
summary: Stockholm institute where Hugo Theorell's laboratory was located.

name: Washington University in St. Louis
summary: University where the Coris' laboratory was located.

name: Rockefeller Institute
summary: New York institute where de Duve was appointed Andrew W. Mellon professor.

name: Albert Einstein College of Medicine
summary: New York college where Alex B. Novikoff worked.

name: International Institute of Cellular and Molecular Pathology
summary: Original name of the institute founded by de Duve in Brussels.

name: Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
summary: Academy that awarded de Duve the Heineken Prize.

name: American Society for Cell Biology
summary: Society that awarded de Duve the E. B. Wilson Award.

name: National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
summary: Academy that elected de Duve a foreign associate.

name: Royal Society of London
summary: Scientific society of which de Duve was a member.

name: United Kingdom
summary: Country where de Duve was born.

name: Thames Ditton
summary: Village near London where de Duve spent his early life.

name: Belgium
summary: Country where de Duve returned in 1920 and spent most of his career.

name: Antwerp
summary: Flemish city where de Duve went to school.

name: France
summary: Country where de Duve served as a medical officer and was taken prisoner.

name: Stockholm
summary: City where de Duve spent a year in Theorell's laboratory.

name: St. Louis
summary: City where de Duve worked at Washington University.

name: New York
summary: Location of Rockefeller Institute and Albert Einstein College of Medicine.

name: Louvain-la-Neuve
summary: Location to which the francophone part of Catholic University of Louvain moved.

name: Brussels
summary: City where de Duve moved with the medical school and founded ICP.

name: lysosome
summary: Organelle discovered by de Duve containing hydrolytic enzymes.

name: peroxisome
summary: Organelle discovered by de Duve characterized by catalase.

name: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
summary: Prize shared by de Duve in 1974.

name: Canada Gairdner International Award
summary: Award received by de Duve in 1967.

name: Dr. H. P. Heineken Prize
summary: Prize received by de Duve in 1973.

name: E. B. Wilson Award
summary: Award received by de Duve in 1989.

name: Viscount
summary: Rank raised to by King Baudouin in 1989.

name: insulin
summary: Hormone de Duve investigated early in his career.

name: glucagon
summary: Hormone discovered as a contaminant in insulin preparations by de Duve.
